physicalNotes: Radius 0.20162404 Jupiter radii from Cointepas et al. 2024 (2024A&A...685A..19C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...685A..19C/abstract): 14,414.5 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.01148418 Jupiter masses (Cointepas et al. 2024, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2024A&A...685A..19C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...685A..19C/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Cointepas et al. 2024 (2024A&A...685A..19C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname COINTEPAS_ET_AL__2024): P 4.6955507 d
sources.shape: Cointepas et al. 2024 (2024A&A...685A..19C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname COINTEPAS_ET_AL__2024): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.0437 au and stellar radius 0.512 solar radii; Cointepas et al. 2024 (2024A&A...685A..19C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname COINTEPAS_ET_AL__2024): inclination 89.3 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Cointepas et al. 2024 (2024A&A...685A..19C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname COINTEPAS_ET_AL__2024): transit mid-time 2458543.40593 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 7 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
